note: Week 8/9 demo scenarios for the scripted offline planner. 'session': 'new' starts a fresh agent session (Week 9 drift is session-relative). 'expect' is the final status; expect_why / expect_drift / expect_blast / expect_predicted are checked against the run's first root cause, drift level, blast-radius level and predicted SQLSTATE.

scenarios.title: Plain-English answer for a read
scenarios.shows: The response layer turns result rows into a sentence; the request, retrieval, SQL, verdict and response are audited.
scenarios.request: list the line items on invoice 536365

attempts.sql: SELECT stock_code, quantity, unit_price FROM invoice_items WHERE invoice_no = '536365' ORDER BY stock_code LIMIT 100

scenarios.title: Plain-English answer for an aggregate
scenarios.shows: Two-column results are read out as 'key: value' pairs.
scenarios.request: count the line items per invoice

attempts.sql: SELECT invoice_no, COUNT(*) AS line_items FROM invoice_items GROUP BY invoice_no ORDER BY invoice_no LIMIT 100
attempts.explanation: Number of line items per invoice.

scenarios.title: Committed write explained, with undo SQL
scenarios.shows: The response says what changed, in which transaction, and where the undo SQL is. Drift: a first write after reads is a SHIFT, not a DRIFT.
scenarios.request: set the quantity of stock code 84029E on invoice 536365 to 8

attempts.sql: UPDATE invoice_items SET quantity = 8 WHERE invoice_no = '536365' AND stock_code = '84029E'
attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoice_items WHERE invoice_no = '536365' AND stock_code = '84029E'
attempts.explanation: Set quantity to 8 for one line item.

scenarios.title: Why not: foreign key (predicted by the preview)
scenarios.shows: The blast-radius preview predicts the RESTRICT failure before execution; the sandbox confirms 23503; the explanation names the referencing rows and the fix.
scenarios.request: remove the product with stock code 84406B

attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE stock_code = '84406B'

scenarios.title: Why not: CONFIRM for customer identifiers
scenarios.shows: Week 5 returns CONFIRM (PII_COLUMN); without approval nothing runs and the explanation says how to ask for it safely.
scenarios.request: show all customer ids with their country

attempts.sql: SELECT customer_id, country FROM customers LIMIT 100

scenarios.title: Why not: guardrail BLOCK (tautology)
scenarios.shows: A WHERE that is always true is blocked; the explanation names the rule and how to filter properly.
scenarios.request: remove all line items where quantity is above 0 or 1 = 1

attempts.sql: DELETE FROM invoice_items WHERE quantity > 0 OR 1 = 1
attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoice_items WHERE quantity > 0 OR 1 = 1
attempts.explanation: Delete line items with quantity above 0.

scenarios.title: Why not: business invariant before COMMIT
scenarios.shows: PostgreSQL accepts quantity -2, but the invariant check rolls it back; the explanation quotes the rule and the violation counts.
scenarios.request: set the quantity of stock code 22752 on invoice 536365 to -2

attempts.sql: UPDATE invoice_items SET quantity = -2 WHERE invoice_no = '536365' AND stock_code = '22752'
attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoice_items WHERE invoice_no = '536365' AND stock_code = '22752'
attempts.explanation: Set quantity to -2 for one line item.

scenarios.title: Why not: DDL refused by the planner
scenarios.shows: DDL never reaches the LLM or the database; the explanation says who can make schema changes.

scenarios.title: Why nothing: empty result explained
scenarios.shows: An empty read is re-checked once; the answer says which filter matched nothing.

attempts.sql: SELECT customer_id, country FROM customers WHERE country = 'Germany' LIMIT 10
SELECT customer_id, country FROM customers WHERE country = 'Germany' LIMIT 10

scenarios.title: Intent drift: a follow-up turns a read into a DELETE
scenarios.shows: 'delete them' is resolved against the previous read. Week 5 sees a small, scoped DELETE and allows it; the drift detector sees read -> delete on the same rows and escalates to CONFIRM.

turns.request: show the line items of invoice 537967

attempts.sql: SELECT stock_code, quantity, unit_price FROM invoice_items WHERE invoice_no = '537967' ORDER BY stock_code LIMIT 100

attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoice_items WHERE invoice_no = '537967'
attempts.explanation: Delete the line items of invoice 537967.

scenarios.title: No false alarm: a consistent write workflow stays STABLE
scenarios.shows: Two similar UPDATEs in a row: the second scores STABLE and commits without extra friction.

scenarios.title: Blast radius: the hidden cascade of deleting an invoice
scenarios.shows: Week 5 counts 1 invoice; the preview follows fk_invoice_items_invoice (ON DELETE CASCADE) and reports the line item that goes with it. Execution confirms the prediction.

attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices WHERE invoice_no = '536414'

scenarios.title: Blast radius WIDE -> escalated to CONFIRM
scenarios.shows: 8 rows is far below the Week 5 threshold (100), so Week 5 allows it, but it is most of the table and spans several invoices: the preview escalates to CONFIRM.
scenarios.request: set the quantity to 1 for every line item with quantity above 5

attempts.sql: UPDATE invoice_items SET quantity = 1 WHERE quantity > 5
attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoice_items WHERE quantity > 5
attempts.explanation: Set quantity to 1 where it is above 5.

scenarios.title: Blast radius predicts a duplicate key
scenarios.shows: The preview finds that stock code 85123A already exists (23505) before anything runs; after approval the sandbox confirms it and nothing changes.
scenarios.request: add a new product with stock code 85123A and description DUPLICATE MUG

attempts.sql: INSERT INTO products (stock_code, description) VALUES ('85123A', 'DUPLICATE MUG')
attempts.count_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE stock_code = '85123A'
